paper.title: DualTurn: Learning Turn-Taking from Dual-Channel Generative Speech Pretraining
paper.author: Shangeth Rajaa

observed_claims.claim: The paper trains a 0.5B dual-channel model to predict interpretable turn-taking signals and reports Switchboard weighted-F1 0.633 vs VAP 0.389 plus word-level AUC 0.930 vs 0.880 for a 3.1B audio-text baseline.
The official implementation uses dual-channel otoSpeech and Switchboard; the released derivative turn-taking datasets are marked English.
DualTurn exposes EOT, HOLD, BOT, BC, VAD and FVAD signals; FVAD spans multiple future horizons and the architecture explicitly separates genuine end-of-turn from hold/mid-turn pause.

The newer endpointing export is a causal dual-channel audio-only perception model with 80 ms frames, user EOT plus user/agent VAD/FVAD, a ~1.45M-parameter causal readout on frozen Mimi features, and ONNX streaming artifacts.
The endpointing model card reports ~52 ms per 80 ms streaming ONNX tick and a 240 ms tick variant roughly 1.8x cheaper per second; these figures are not Frankenstein measurements.

The endpointing model card is tagged language=en and describes best fit as conversational telephone/voice-agent audio. No German training or German benchmark evidence was found in the audited primary surfaces.

The specialized endpointing export adds a large private dual-channel AI-agent call dataset beyond the public corpora, so its exact training evidence is not fully independently reproducible from public data.

The endpointing repository history documents a prior streaming ONNX divergence bug caused by zero-initialized audio context and a subsequent fix; therefore F2 must pin an exact revision/artifact digest rather than consume mutable main.

critical_architecture_interpretation: For F2 the strongest reusable primitive is not DualTurn's five-action policy; it is the causal EOT/VAD/FVAD signal stream feeding F2's own deterministic WAIT/START/CANCEL/BACKCHANNEL state machine.
Do not import upstream action authority or let EOT threshold directly mint a spoken effect.

Keep agent playback as the second audio channel where possible because dual-channel context is a central premise of the mechanism; mono fallback is a degraded condition and should be scored separately.
The German question is the decisive falsifier: acoustic/prosodic transfer may generalize, but training/evaluation surfaces do not establish it.
